title: Tactical Battle of Navsari (c. 738 CE)
disclaimer: Schematic tactical battlefield plate, not a survey. Tactical positions based on the Navsari Copperplate Grant (738-739 CE).

map.attribution: Original schematic tactical battlefield plate. Purna River, coastal estuary, and Navsari earthworks. North is up.

scenes.title: The Umayyad Army Marches South
scenes.narration: In 738 CE, having devastated northern frontier kingdoms, the main southern army of the Umayyad Caliphate under General Al-Hakam marched forty-five thousand cavalry and infantry south toward the Deccan, seeking to conquer the Indian heartland.
scenes.speech: In 738 CE, having devastated northern frontier kingdoms, the main southern army of the Umayyad Caliphate under General Al-Hakam marched forty-five thousand cavalry and infantry south toward the Deccan, seeking to conquer the Indian heartland.

scenes.title: Pulakeshin's Army Ready at the Purna
scenes.narration: At the Purna River before Navsari, Chalukya viceroy Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin stood ready with thirty-five thousand veteran warriors. With massive war elephants anchoring the center and cavalry masking the wings, the Indian battle line was formed and waiting.
scenes.speech: At the Purna River before Navsari, Chalukya viceroy Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin stood ready with thirty-five thousand veteran warriors. With massive war elephants anchoring the center and cavalry masking the wings, the Indian battle line was formed and waiting.

scenes.title: The Decisive Clash at Navsari Ford
scenes.narration: The Arab vanguard funneled into the narrow river crossing, expecting a quick breakthrough. Instead, Pulakeshin unleashed a devastating counter-charge. War elephants crashed into the Arab ranks, breaking cavalry formations in the muddy riverbed.
scenes.speech: The Arab vanguard funneled into the narrow river crossing, expecting a quick breakthrough. Instead, Pulakeshin unleashed a devastating counter-charge. War elephants crashed into the Arab ranks, breaking cavalry formations in the muddy riverbed.

scenes.title: Caliphate Army Annihilated & General Slain
scenes.narration: Enveloped against the tidal marshes, the Caliphate army broke into catastrophic rout. General Al-Hakam was slain in the melee, and over twenty-five thousand Tajika invaders fell or were captured, completely shattering the invasion force.
scenes.speech: Enveloped against the tidal marshes, the Caliphate army broke into catastrophic rout. General Al-Hakam was slain in the melee, and over twenty-five thousand Tajika invaders fell or were captured, completely shattering the invasion force.

scenes.title: The Bulwark of India Victorious
scenes.narration: The victory at Navsari was absolute. Crowned the Repeller of the Tajikas, Pulakeshin secured the Deccan with moderate losses, while Nagabhata locked Rajasthan. Together, these Indian monarchs smashed the invasion and shielded India for three centuries.
scenes.speech: The victory at Navsari was absolute. Crowned the Repeller of the Tajikas, Pulakeshin secured the Deccan with moderate losses, while Nagabhata locked Rajasthan. Together, these Indian monarchs smashed the invasion and shielded India for three centuries.

lines: BATTLE OF NAVSARI (c. 738 CE) — COMPLETE TRIUMPH
Indian Commander: Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin (~35,000 troops, ~6,000 casualties)
Invader General: Al-Hakam ibn Awana († KIA, ~25,000+ casualties, army annihilated)
Allied Northern Victor: Nagabhata I (Gurjara-Pratihara) — India Shielded for 300 Years

sources.text: The Navsari Inscription (738-739 CE) records that the Tajika (Arab) army, having destroyed the kingdoms of Saindhava, Kachchella, Saurashtra, Chavotkata, and Maurya, attempted to penetrate the Deccan. Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin, Chalukya viceroy of Gujarat, met them at Navsari and annihilated their forces, earning the title 'Tajikanivaraka'.
refs: Mirashi, V. V., Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum, Vol. IV (Inscriptions of the Kalachuri-Chedi Era)
Bhandarkar, D. R., Indian Antiquary, Vol. XVII

sources.text: The Gwalior Prasasti of Bhoja I records that Nagabhata I crushed the large invading Mlechchha (Arab) army in Rajasthan and Malwa, serving as a divine bulwark against the foreign host.
refs: Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XVIII (Gwalior Inscription of Bhoja I)
Majumdar, R. C., The Classical Age (The History and Culture of the Indian People)
